question: Four times P’s present age exceeds Q’s present age by 41 years. After 10 years, three times Q’s age will be 33 years less than seven times P’s age at that time. What is Q’s present age?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use option verification for the fastest result.

Test Option 2: Let Q's present age = 63 years.

From statement 1: 4P = 63 + 41 = 104 ⇒ P = 26 years.

Ages after 10 years: Q = 73 years, P = 36 years.

Check statement 2: 3 × 73 = 219 and (7 × 36) − 33 = 252 − 33 = 219. (Condition satisfies)

**∴ The correct answer is 63 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Eq 1: 4P − Q = 41
 Eq 2: 3(Q + 10) = 7(P + 10) − 33

**Given:**

⇒ Present age condition: 4P − Q = 41 ... (Equation 1)

⇒ Future age condition: 3(Q + 10) = 7(P + 10) − 33 ... (Equation 2)

**Calculations:**

⇒ From Equation 1, we get: Q = 4P − 41

⇒ Expanding Equation 2:

⇒ 3Q + 30 = 7P + 70 − 33

⇒ 3Q + 30 = 7P + 37

⇒ 3Q = 7P + 7

⇒ Substitute Q = 4P − 41 into the simplified Equation 2:

⇒ 3(4P − 41) = 7P + 7

⇒ 12P − 123 = 7P + 7

⇒ 12P − 7P = 123 + 7

⇒ 5P = 130

⇒ P = 26 years

⇒ Now, substitute P = 26 into Equation 1:

⇒ Q = 4(26) − 41

⇒ Q = 104 − 41 = 63 years

**∴ The correct answer is 63 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Ages

The age difference between two individuals always remains constant regardless of the time period (past, present, or future).

Ratio of Ages

If the current age ratio is a : b, their ages are taken as ax and bx. After n years, their ages become (ax + n) and (bx + n).

Average Age Property

If the average age of n people is A, then after k years, the new average age of the same group will naturally become A + k.
